description: The palaeogeography of the Bass Strait land-bridge, a vital zone of human and biological connectivity across southeastern Australia is a series of datasets listed in Australian national open data portal, an open data portal, published or maintained by Geoscience Australia Data. Land-bridges are key regions of human connectivity, yet how geography affected peoples' movement during flooding is poorly understood. Bass Strait is one of the most important land-bridges in Australasia, separating Lutruwita/Tasmania from the mainland of Australia. Coverage: Australia. The portal lists 9 near-identical datasets in this series (one per year, month, area or site), grouped in this record; the first few are linked. The portal files it under the publisher Geoscience Australia Data. Its tags are Australia-wide geoscience data, First Nations, Geomorphology and earth surface processes, Offshore Mapping, Physiography. It offers 1 resource(s) in HTML. The portal shows 2026-05-14 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the portal listing (dataset page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support traffic, parking and road network studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-ckan-au-portal.
